af6323cccb.q: What are the most critical clauses mental health providers should review before signing an insurance contract?
af6323cccb.a: Tom Tarshish identifies four key contract elements to review: (1) a mutual termination clause allowing either party to exit with reasonable notice—the most important protection; (2) the number of days allowed to file claims; (3) the timeline and process for insurance payment disputes and recoupment; (4) arbitration location and whether it can be conducted by video. He emphasizes that as long as a reasonable termination clause exists, providers have limited risk, since they can exit if payments or service become problematic.

1cf800fce1.q: Why is monitoring Medicare rate changes important even for cash-pay mental health practices?
1cf800fce1.a: Tom Tarshish explains that Medicare sets reimbursement rates for all physicians and therapists, and proposed changes in 2027 could significantly hurt providers. He notes that Medicare has not kept up with inflation and Congress has empowered CMS to set rates without congressional approval. Even cash-pay practices should monitor these changes because they establish industry benchmarks and affect the entire healthcare economy. The CMS comment deadline is September 14th, with major physician groups like the American Medical Association actively lobbying against harmful proposals.
